place.source_title: Richard Talbott House, 301 West Second Street

brief: One of the oldest houses in town (1819-20): a two-storey, three-bay Federal brick house raised over a fully exposed basement, side-gabled with end chimneys, shuttered 6/6 windows and a stoop with iron rails; a rear addition was built in the 1870s. Record: 2 photos plus 6 measured drawing sheets.

facade.notes: the Richard Talbott House (1820), Federal: two storeys of painted brick on a high basement, built right on the sidewalk, a stoop with iron rails, shutters, end chimneys, ivy on one wall; a plainer brick house of the same height across the side street; a narrow street

why.note: a pre-1850 river-town lot: the house on the front line, the yard behind
Ohio River floods: living floors raised over a high basement
